newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian rebels dynamite main oil pipeline again.
newsitem.headline: Colombian rebels dynamite main oil pipeline again.

text.p: Leftist rebels dynamited Colombia's main oil pipeline for the ninth time this year leading to the spillage of between 8,000 and 9,000 barrels of crude, a spokesman for the state oil company Ecopetrol said on Monday.

The attack took place near the town of Arauquita, in northeast Arauca province, on Sunday evening. Pumping operations were suspended but the Ecopetrol spokesman said repairs would be completed by late Monday or early Tuesday.
The pipeline runs from the Cano Limon oil field to the lifting terminal at Covenas on the Caribbean coast. It is operated by Occidental Petroleum Corp of the United States.
The pipeline has the capacity to pump 200,000 barrels of crude per day.
Last year it was blown up 47 times by the National Liberation Army (ELN), Colombia's second largest rebel force which specializes in attacks on oil infrastructure.
At least 105,000 barrels were spilled in the attacks, which cost about $9.3 million in repairs and clean up operations. Pumping was suspended for 46 days in 1996, according to an Ecopetrol report.
